novelty_flags.label: Bibliography, literature checklist, and related_work: TehSadeghiSoo2025Robust
novelty_flags.one_line: The core calls the paper an ICML Workshop publication, but the inspected published version is an ICML 2025 proceedings paper; correct the venue/version while retaining the accurately described sufficient-only result.

soundness_flags.label: Theorems 1–2
soundness_flags.one_line: “Certified input” is not defined to require a nonempty represented family and a realizable exact-oracle locus, yet D0 and the asserted rational separator require both; add D≠∅ and MExact≠∅ (or an explicit infeasibility branch).

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 3
soundness_flags.one_line: Uniformity over “certified fixed inputs” is undefined while m, the rational circuit, output dimension, and derivative bounds vary; state a fixed finite input or a uniformly bounded indexed class with a precise sandwich estimator.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 2
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: SparseSIM-ID completeness is conditional on the rational-positive separation assertion of Theorem 1.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The headline completeness claim is “complete for realizable nonempty tied-sparsest inputs, conditional on Theorem 1,” while Theorem 1 remains the project’s primary to-prove contribution.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1 publication header; Section 4.2, p. 4; proof of Theorem 3.2, pp. 7–8
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published paper presents a sufficient criterion for simultaneous identification and says that necessity needs a common density Markov to all candidate SA-MPDAGs with unequal graphwise effects; it is not an ICML Workshop paper.
The paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion and a causal identification formula for one MPDAG.
IDGraphs recursively enumerates minimal subclasses and distinct total-effect functionals within one MPDAG.
The paper supplies a complete identification algorithm and graphical nonidentifiability characterization for one PAG.
Autobounds compiles discrete causal queries into polynomial programs, supplies sharp bounds at completion, and maintains valid outer bounds during computation.
The paper constructs post-discovery confidence sets by resampling/screening and unions of graphwise intervals, with asymptotic coverage for a fixed population effect.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a realizable certified-input class with D nonempty and MExact nonempty, and make infeasible CI bit-vectors a separately certified rejection branch.
Replace Theorem 3’s informal uniformity with either a fixed-input delta-method theorem or explicit bounds on m, denominator margins, circuit derivatives, and the plug-in sandwich estimator.
Correct Teh et al.’s venue and add a theorem-level strictness corollary showing a tied-sparsest instance where its graphical test is undecided but SparseSIM-ID returns the rational separator.
Turn the atlas question into a constructive proof program by specifying chart primitives and proving a bound first for a restricted class such as bounded-treewidth tied DAGs.

recommended_next_step: Revise the input-domain and inference quantifiers, correct the Teh citation, then advance the realizable tied-sparsest rational-separation kernel to Stage 0.
